newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees petrochemical demand rising.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees petrochemical demand rising.

text.p: Indonesia's demand for paraxylene, purified terepthalic acid (PTA) and ethylene are expected to rise in 1998, an official from the state oil company Pertamina said on Tuesday.

Giyanto Hadipurnomo, general manager in Pertamina's gas and petrochemicals division, said at a petrochemicals conference that demand for paraxylene was expected to rise to 1.2 million tonnes in 1998 from 950,000 tonnes in 1997.
Indonesia's paraxylene supply was forecast to be only 640,000 tonnnes in 1998, compared with 270,000 tonnes in 1997.

Hadipurnomo said PTA demand was expected to rise to 1.03 million tonnes in 1998 from 930,000 tonnes in 1997. PTA supply should rise to 1.77 million tonnes in 1998 from 1.42 million tonnes in 1997, he added.
He said ethylene demand was forecast to rise to 955,000 tonnes in 1998 from 762,000 tonnes in 1997.
He said ethylene supply would be 600,000 tonnes in 1998 compared with 550,000 tonnes in 1997.

"Indonesia is a potential market because of growing demand for petrochemical products. This demand will be fulfilled by domestic manufacturers as well as imports from other countries," Hadipurnomo said.
Paraxylene, PTA and ethylene are used as raw materials in the plastics and textiles industries.
